stem.text: Selected values of a function f are given in the table. The function f is not defined at \( x = 3 \). What does the table suggest about \( \lim_{x \to 3} f(x) \)?

answer_key.label: The table suggests that the limit does not exist, because the outputs approach different values on the two sides of x = 3.

worked_solution.text: From the left, the outputs 3.1500, 3.9195, 3.9920, 3.9992 approach 4.
worked_solution.rule_named: reading a table from one side

worked_solution.text: From the right, the outputs -0.4500, -0.0405, -0.0040, -0.0004 approach 0.
worked_solution.rule_named: reading a table from one side

worked_solution.text: The two sides approach different values, so the table suggests the two sided limit does not exist.
worked_solution.rule_named: two sided limit exists only when the one sided limits agree

options.label: The table suggests that the limit does not exist, because the outputs approach different values on the two sides of x = 3.
The table suggests that the limit is 0, because the outputs approach 0 from the right of x = 3.
options.derivation: the value the right hand rows approach reported as the two sided limit
